patches.replace: PROLOGUS ALTER EX LIBRIS BEATI AUGUSTI. <hi>Qualiter
patches.why: DIGITIZATION SILENTLY REPAIRED MIGNE, PLATE READ 2026-09-21 (archive patrologiaecurs29goog leaf n314, corners 599/600; map leaf = (col + 29)/2, calibrated at n310 = 591/592 and n317 = 605/606). The head of the second prologue sets 'Ex libris beati AUGUSTI.' in small caps, with a full stop, read on a full-resolution crop. Corpus Corporum prints AUGUSTINI with a comma. Augustine is plainly meant: the prologue cites Aug. l. xx contr. Faust. c. 21 in its first sentence. But the plate prints a REAL word, so this is Pattern 18 [cj:] business in the English and never a silent repair in the Latin. Punctuation restored with it (Pattern 8).
